recap.workouts:
Prescribed today: FULL REST. Logged: a 36:21 road ride — 13.95 km, 176 W average, HR 133 avg / 151 max, load 29, off the Garmin, unpaired to any planned session because there wasn't one. Nothing came through from the phone — no note, no log, the sync is still sitting on Saturday — so the stream is the whole story.

I read the per-second watts against your current bands (FTP 236 W). The 36.4 minutes split: 4.5 min sub-Z1 coasting, 3.9 min Z1, 11.9 min Z2 — and then 11.9 min of Zone X (196–222 W), 3.0 min Z3, 0.6 min Z4, 0.8 min Z5. So 16.3 of 36.4 minutes, 45% of the ride, sat at or above the one band the plan tells you to avoid.

The shape shows exactly where it went. Five-minute averages: 169 W to open, then 192, 206, 193, 199 — a straight quarter of an hour parked on the Z2/Zone-X line — then 155, 138, 78 W rolling home. This wasn't a hard ride. It was a ride with no target on it, and on rolling ground that defaults to medium.

The heart-rate side is the good news, and it is genuinely good. HR settled at 132–137 and stayed there through the entire middle block, flat, never drifting upward while the watts held. Max 151 — eight beats under bike LTHR 159 — and that peak is a single spike (610 W max, so one sprint or one steep pitch), not sustained work. 199 W at HR 137 with no drift is a very comfortable place to be at 84% of FTP. A week after CT31 set it, the 236 W anchor is looking honest.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: aerobically clean, tactically the most expensive 36 minutes of the week. There is no fatigue flag anywhere in the trace — flat HR at 132–137, 22 beats under LTHR while holding 199 W, no drift, no decoupling story to tell. But 11.9 minutes of Zone X on a prescribed rest day is single-handedly the biggest reason week 8 finished 75.2% easy against the 80% target. Zone X costs like hard work and pays like easy work. Confidence: high — read off the full per-second stream.

2) The lesson isn't "don't ride." It's that a ride with no band on it finds Zone X by itself. Same 36 minutes, same road, a 196 W ceiling on the head unit, and week 8 clears 80/20. That's a number you set before you roll out, not willpower you summon at minute 15.

3) ADAPT: no-op. Week 8 closes tonight and week 9 was generated today with this ride already counted in the polarization audit, so there is nothing left in the week to move. Nothing gets added to a week that's over.

4) Tomorrow is the same test wearing a uniform. CF9 is 50 minutes at 165–196 W on the new anchor — and 196 is the ceiling, not the target.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
CAn4 — 90' on the bike: 10' Z1, then 6 × (2:30 Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 5:00 Z1), 30' Zone 2 @ 165–196 W, 5' Z1. Both bands are the post-CT31 numbers (FTP 236 W). No gym, no class — Saturday is bike only.

Coach's call, decided on tomorrow morning's numbers rather than tonight's: this is the last item on the week's list and the plan's own designated first full cut. If readiness is still down in the twenties, either drop it outright or ride only the 30' Z2 tail — six Z4 reps is the single biggest block of hard time left in a week whose entire job was to deload. If you wake up genuinely normal, ride it as written and keep the recoveries as lazy as today's were.

Sunday is full rest either way. That part isn't negotiable.

recovery.bannerTitle: Week 9 seeded — the build opens tomorrow
recovery.bannerSub: Seven endurance sessions, 8:55 of bike and run, two hard stimuli (Wed CMI1, Fri RCI8), and the banked load bumps now spent. Week 8 came in at 75.2% easy against the 80% target — the fix is volume and staying out of Zone X, not more restraint. Monday's morning run replaces this line with live readiness.
recovery.note: Readiness 24 — the lowest of the block, off 27 twice. Here's the honest tension, and I'd rather name it than smooth it: the load side of the ledger finally did what it was supposed to. Week 8 closed ~426 against week 7's 456, ATL is falling, Form is the shallowest it has been in ten days, and yesterday's CAn4 was a clean six-rep set with HR flattening exactly at LTHR and ~30 beats shed in every recovery. None of that is a fatigued athlete. And yet the overnight signals went the wrong way across that same week: sleeping HR 58 → 61 → 63 → 64 → 64 → 63 → 65 (3-night smooth 64.0 vs a 57.5 baseline) and respiratory rate now 14.4 against 13.4, worse than yesterday and worse than Thursday. Two autonomic markers drifting up THROUGH a genuine deload is not what accumulated training load looks like — it's what an early bug, or life stress, or a hot bedroom looks like. Wrist temp ticked 35.61 → 35.90 but is still under the flag threshold, so I'm not calling it illness; I'm calling it watch-it, second week running. What I'd weight today: sleep. 6.11 h ending at 03:29 is the second truncated night in three, the 7-night average is 7.2 h against a need of 8, and both exports this morning carry the identical stage list, so 03:29 is a real wake, not a sync artefact. Rest is already the plan — the only thing you can actually get wrong today is treating a rest day as a free day and going to bed late again. Tomorrow opens the Week 9 build; the deload earned that, but the overnight numbers haven't yet agreed, and today's plan-gen should hear from you how you actually feel before it commits.

2026-08-03.mind: Today the discipline is restraint: 165 to 196 watts will feel firmer than last week's numbers because the anchor moved, not because I got weaker — I hold the band and hand the rest of the week fresh legs.

end.name: CMI1 — THE WEEK'S SESSION (mixed intervals)
end.desc:
20′ Z1 → 2 × (20′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W / 15′ Z1) → 10 × (1′ Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 2′ Z1). (Pulled from the live 80/20 library 2 Aug — structure verbatim. The Z4 set comes AFTER the threshold blocks and the workout ends on the last recovery; add 5′ easy to close if you want it.)
The two 20′ blocks are the point — the ten Z4 reps are a top-up on already-tired legs and are meant to feel harder than the watts suggest.
40 minutes of Z3 is double anything you have ridden this block and it is your first threshold work on the new 236 W anchor, so target the low half of the band, 222–235 W, on block 1. If HR plateaus clearly under 159, ride block 2 a touch firmer; if HR is at or above 159 by minute 12 of block 1, hold the watts and let it sit there.
Set the effort in the first 5 minutes of each block and stop adjusting — one early correction, never a stair-step (the 28 Jul CT31 lesson).
On-bike gate for the Z4 set: if you cannot get back to Z1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or rep power falls below 248 W, stop the set and spin out the remainder. Seven good reps is a completed session; ten bad ones is how week 7 ended.

2026-08-06.mind: Yesterday was the work and today is how I keep it — seventy-five boring minutes under 165 watts, and every watt I add out of impatience is one I steal from Friday.

cf.name: Rogers (AMRAP 30) — scale to a pace you can hold
cf.desc:
Rogers — AMRAP 30: 400 m run + 8 bar or ring muscle-ups + 500/450 m row + 15 DB bench press 50/35. (Run counts as 1 rep.)
Call: scale to a volume you can hold at conversational pace for the full 30 minutes — cut the muscle-ups to a number you can do near-unbroken (or sub jumping/banded), jog the 400s honestly slow, steady on the row.
Today's endurance is a pure Zone 1 spin BECAUSE this exists. Race a 30-minute AMRAP and the spin cannot do its job, and Friday's threshold run inherits the debt.

end.name: CRe10 — 75′ pure recovery spin
end.desc:
75′ Zone 1 @ 118–165 W.
Pure recovery. No Zone 2 creep, no "it felt easy so I lifted it." Its entire value is being boring the day after CMI1 — and Rogers has already taken a bite out of the morning.

2026-08-07.mind: These are the first threshold reps on a threshold I actually measured, so I run the effort and let the terrain move the pace — four honest six-minute blocks, no hero splits.

cf.name: Front Squat 1×1 + Reeves (AMRAP 9) — capped · PROTECT THE RUN

Reeves — AMRAP 9: 45 double unders + 15 wall balls 20/14. [FITNESS]: 75 single unders + 15 wall balls 16/12.
Call: front squats capped ~85%, singles only, stop the moment bar speed drops — and RCI8 runs later today. Reeves is only 9 minutes: take the [FITNESS] wall balls and keep the double unders relaxed. Heavy front squats + wall balls + 4 × 6′ at threshold pace is exactly the leg-stacking pattern the mandate names as hypothesis #1.

2026-08-08.mind: The whole job today is refusing to drift — five-oh-one to five-forty-five and not a second quicker, because a long run run medium is the exact mistake that empties a week.

end.name: RF12 — long easy run
end.desc:
5′ Z1 → 80′ Zone 2 @ 5:01–5:45/km → 5′ Z1.
The week's long run, the day after a threshold run, and it must stay in the band. Drifting into the 4:50s makes it Zone X — the exact "medium" that wrecks an 80/20 week.

2026-08-09.mind: Half an hour of Zone 1 before I am allowed to touch Zone 2 — the plan wrote it that way on purpose, and finishing a seven-day week easy is what makes the next one possible.

Ride it as written; the long easy lead-in is the point on a seventh consecutive training day. No gym, no class, just the bike.
